The lantern room smelled of warm metal even though the lamp had been dark for years. Rain had worked its way through the upper windows, leaving thin mineral tracks on the curved glass. Below the stairs, the coast road vanished into a fold of cloud. Quinn set a toolbox on the floor and tested the handrail before putting any weight on it.

“We can mend the frame before evening,” said Quinn. She spread a cloth beneath the damaged hinge and arranged the screws in a line. A note from Ivo lay under the toolbox, weighted with a stone. It described the old mechanism carefully but offered no explanation for the blue thread caught inside it. Quinn put the thread in an envelope instead of brushing it away with the dust.

The lower part of the frame moved freely. At the top, something resisted every gentle turn. Quinn climbed down to fetch a smaller driver, counting the narrow steps to keep from thinking about the drop beyond the glass. On the landing, an unopened parcel waited beside a coil of rope. The address had faded until only the number of the lighthouse remained readable.

Quinn lifted the parcel onto the bench. “That can wait until the hinge is safe.” She returned to the stairs with the smaller tool tucked into a pocket. The metal gave a brief click as the stubborn screw loosened. Behind it, a sliver of painted wood fell onto the cloth. One side carried a tiny white star; the other was rough and unpainted.

For a while, the only movement in the room came from the rain. Quinn compared the sliver with the wood around the window and found no matching surface. It must have arrived with the thread, perhaps in a repair made before Ivo kept the light. The possibility made the room feel less abandoned. Somebody had worked patiently here, keeping the weather outside one small adjustment at a time.

“I will leave a record this time,” said Quinn. She wrote the date on the envelope and drew the shape of the sliver beside it. Then she tightened the hinge, closed the window, and waited until the frame held still against the wind.
